title: Guidelines for Renewal of Certificate of Registration for Drug Products Human and Vet 2024

1.0. General
1.1. The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has the
responsibility of ensuring that all drug products placed on the Nigerian market
for use meet the requirements for Quality, Safety and Efficacy throughout
the life cycle of the product.
1.2. The procedure for renewal of the license of all drug products outlines the
process to be followed and the technical requirements to be met before a
product can be continually placed on the Nigerian market.
1.3. A product authorized for marketing in Nigeria will be issued a Certificate
of Registration valid for 5 years and should be continually renewed upon
expiration.
1.4. These guidelines are intended to provide guidance on the technical and
other general data requirements when applying for renewal of product
license for all drug products.
1.5. NAFDAC will not entertain renewal application for the registration of
imported regulated products on the Federal Government Import Prohibition
List, NAFDAC Ceiling List and NAFDAC 5 + 5 List.
1.6. NOTE: These Guidelines should be read in conjunction with all relevant ICH
guidance documents including the following;
a. ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline Pharmaceutical Quality System Q10
https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/Q10%20Guideline.pdf
b. ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline “Quality Risk Management Q9(R2)”
https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/Q9_Guideline.pdf
c. ICH Harmonised Guideline Technical and Regulatory considerations for
Pharmaceutical Product Lifecycle Management Q12
https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/Q12_Guideline_Step4_2019_1
119.pdf
Step I
2.0. Application Letter for Renewal of Product Licence
2.1. An application for renewal should be initiated not later than six (6) months
to the date of expiration of the current/valid Licence with PSUR submitted
to Pharmacovigiliance Directorate for review.
2.2. An application for the renewal of all drug products should be submitted and
processed on the NAFDAC Automated Product Administration and Monitoring
System (NAPAMS) portal - https://registration.nafdac.gov.ng. For more
information see the NAPAMS User Manual
2.3. The renewal application should be addressed
To: The Director-General

2.4. A separate application form should be submitted for each product.
Step II
3.0. Documentation
The following documents are the requirements for submission of an application for
renewal of product license.
3.1. Annual License/Premises Registration
The current Annual Licence to practice and the Certificate of Retention of
Premises for the Superintendent Pharmacist issued by the Pharmacy Council
of Nigeria (PCN)should be submitted.
3.2. Manufacturing Licence
3.2.1. Issued by a relevant health/regulatory body in the country of
manufacture (For products manufactured outside Nigeria).
3.2.2. Be authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy or High Commission in
the country of origin. In countries where no Nigerian embassy
exists, any Commonwealth or ECOWAS country can authenticate.
3.2.3. Indicate Name and address of manufacturer and the products to
be registered.
3.3. Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (COPP-WHO Format)
3.3.1. Issued by a relevant health/regulatory body in the country of
manufacturer (For products manufactured outside Nigeria).
3.3.2. Be authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy or High Commission in the
country of origin. In countries where no Nigerian embassy exists, any
Commonwealth or ECOWAS country can authenticate. Indicate Name
and address of manufacturer and the products to be registered.
3.4. Evidence of expired or about to expire NAFDAC license
A copy of the expired Certificate of Registration for the product (s).
3.5. Evidence of Registration of Brand Name/Trademark
Evidence of Registration of Brand Name with Trademark Registry in the
Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. This should be done in the name

3.6. Notarized Declaration
A declaration by the applicant regarding the correctness, completeness and
accuracy of all documents submitted should be provided. The format should be
in line with the template attached as Annex 2 in this guideline. This document
must be notarized by a notary public.
3.7. Power of Attorney/Contract Manufacturing Agreement (where
applicable) At the expiration of a product license, the Power of Attorney or
Contract Manufacturing Agreement may have lapsed except in cases when
a specific expiration date was specified in the original power of attorney or
contract manufacturing agreement or a statement that the power of attorney
is for an indefinite period. Except in the cases stated above, an Applicant will
be required to submit a new power of attorney or contract manufacturing
agreement at renewal.
The document shall give details of:
3.7.1. The Issuer and the Receiver of the Power of Attorney and in the case
of a Contract Manufacturing Agreement, the parties involved with
their specific roles and the terms of the contract agreement.
3.7.2. A list of the products covered by the Power of Attorney (this can come
as an annexure for large number of products but must form part of
the power of attorney with a specific reference to the annexure
stated on the Power of Attorney).
3.7.3. State ownership of Brand name/s or Trademark.
3.7.4. The validity of the Power of Attorney should be stated, and it should
not be less than 5 years.
3.7.5. The document must be signed by the authorized person(s) and should
be notarized by a Notary Public in the country of manufacture.
3.8. List of Approved Variations for the product and the approval
letters (where applicable). This should indicate the type of variations
and respective dates of approval.
3.9. Product Quality Review (PQR) and current Quality Information
Summary (QIS)
Step III.
4.0 Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP)

For Information on the Inspection of manufacturing facility, Applicant should visit
the Drug Evaluation and Research (DER) Directorate section of the Agency’s
website. The GMP status of the manufacturing facility will be considered before the
renewal of the product license is issued.
Step IV
5.0 Issuance of Notice of Renewal
5.1. Upon satisfactory review of submitted documents and satisfactory GMP, a
Notice of Renewal (NOR) shall be issued.
Step V
6.0 Submission of laboratory samples:
6.1. For Imported products, samples for laboratory analysis should be submitted
while samples will be drawn for locally manufactured products during the GMP
Inspection.
6.2. The following documents are required;
6.2.1. Letter for submission of laboratory samples.
6.2.2. Evidence of payment of processing fee.
6.2.3. Certificate of analysis.
The Certificate of Analysis must be presented on a letter-head of the
quality control laboratory where the sample was tested/evaluated
and should contain the under-listed information:
6.2.3.1. The brand name of the product
6.2.3.2.The batch number of the product
6.2.3.3.The manufacturing and expiry dates
6.2.3.4.The name, designation, and signature of the Analyst
6.2.3.5.A copy of Notice of Renewal
6.2.3.6 The Analytical method used in the product analysis and the
Analytical Method Validation as contained in the product
dossier
Step VI
7.0 Product Approval meeting
Upon meeting all regulatory requirements, product is presented for Approval
Meeting.
Step VII
8.0 Issuance of Certificate
For products approved at the meeting, an electronic certificate of Renewal of
Product Registration is issued to the applicant.

The product label at renewal should be the same as first approval unless an

10.0 Tariff
Please see NAFDAC Tariff section of the Agency’s website.
11.0 Note
11.0. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the disqualification
of the renewal application or lead to considerable delay in the renewal
process.
11.1. A successful renewal application will be issued a Certificate of Registration
with a validity period of another five (5) years.
11.2. Renewal of Registration of a product does not automatically confer
Advertising Permit. A separate application and subsequent approval by the
Agency shall be required if the product is to be advertised. Simultaneous
submission of renewal and advertisement applications are not allowed.
11.3. NAFDAC reserves the right to revoke, suspend or vary a certificate during its
validity period.
11.4. Filing an application form or paying an application fee does not confer
renewal of license status.
11.5. Failure to respond promptly to queries or enquiries raised by NAFDAC on the
renewal application (within 45 working days) will automatically lead to the
closure of the Application.
11.6. The timeline for Renewal of Certificate of Product Registration from
acceptance of submissions to issuance of Registration number is ninety (90)
working days.
11.7. Please note that the clock stops once compliances are issued.

Annex 1
Product Quality Review (PQR)
1.0 A product quality review should be submitted with the objective of verifying the
consistency of the quality of the Finished Pharmaceutical Product and its
manufacturing process.
2.0 Rejected batches should not be included in the analysis but must be reported
separately, and together with the reports of failure investigations, as indicated
below.
3.0 Reviews should include at least:
1. a review of starting and primary packaging materials used in the FPP, especially
those from new sources;
2. a tabulated review and statistical analysis of quality control and in-process control
results;
3. a review of all batches that failed to meet established specification(s);
4. a review of all critical deviations or non-conformances and related investigations.
5. a review of all changes carried out to the processes or analytical methods.
6. a review of the results of the stability-monitoring programme;
7. a review of all quality-related returns, complaints and recalls, including export-
only medicinal products.
8. a review of the adequacy of previous corrective actions.
9. a list of validated analytical and manufacturing procedures and their revalidation
dates.
10. Review of all adverse drug reactions observed, and action taken- to be
submitted to Pharmacovigilance Directorate. (Part of PSUR review)
11. Review of Periodic Risk-Benefit Evaluation (PBRER) Reports- to be submitted to
Pharmacovigilance Directorate. (Part of PSUR review).
12. Review of Post-Marketing Surveillance activities- to be submitted to
Pharmacovigilance Directorate. (Part of PSUR review).
Further Notes
1. Reviews must include data from all batches manufactured during the review period.
2. Data should be presented in tabular or graphical form, when applicable.
3. The above listing of requirements is specific to the p r o d u c t q u a l i t y
r e v i e w requirements and does not relieve the applicant of related GMP
requirements.
